text: Kingsmoor FC a pris un bon départ grâce à Viktor Quinlan, auteur de deux buts au début, dont un penalty (1 but attendu à 0,76, un peu plus de 7 chances sur 10) [#152] [#222]. Mais Westport Albion a répliqué rapidement avec Rafael Delacroix, qui a marqué deux fois avec des tirs proches de la réussite quasi assurée (1 but attendu à 0,97, presque sûr à rentrer) [#401] [#553]. En seconde période, Kenji Rahman a égalisé pour Westport (xG 0,69, chance forte) [#983], avant que Luca Iversen ne rende la pareille pour Kingsmoor malgré un joueur en moins suite à un carton rouge [#1516] [#1495]. Westport a eu plus d'occasions (18 tirs contre 10) et une meilleure qualité d'actions (xG 3,77 contre 3,06), mais n'a pas su garder son avantage. Kingsmoor a joué large en attaquant sur les côtés et a su ajuster son pressing, tandis que Westport a alterné entre jeu direct et contrôle du rythme [#1187] [#1459]. Ce match est un vrai régal pour les amoureux du suspense et du jeu offensif !

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in fr

- Viktor Quinlan scored twice early on for Kingsmoor FC with xG 0.76 (penalty) and 0.266, setting initial lead for his team [#152, #222].
- Rafael Delacroix equalized and then gave Westport Albion a 2-2 lead with two high xG goals of 0.768 and 0.973 in the first half [#401, #553].
- Westport Albion's Kenji Rahman scored the important equalizer at 51' with an xG of 0.693, leveling the score again [#983].
- Kingsmoor FC's Luca Iversen scored late at 82' with an xG of 0.868, making it 3-3 after Felix Barros from Kingsmoor was sent off with a second yellow card at 81' [#1516, #1495].
- Westport Albion dominated shots (18 to 10) and shots on target (11 to 3) with higher xG (3.77 to 3.06), but the match ended in a 3-3 draw [team_stats].

- Kingsmoor FC's opening goals followed a pattern of patient build-up play exploiting wide areas consistent with their 4-4-2 wide crossing style. For example, the 12' goal by Viktor Quinlan was created after an 8-pass sequence lasting 26.7 seconds starting from a ball regain, involving multiple midfield and wide players culminating in a finish inside 9m, showing effective use of width and crossing support [#222].
- Westport Albion responded with direct, vertical passing sequences characteristic of their style. Their 22' goal involved 7 quick passes over 25.8 seconds starting from a regain, finished close to goal after a short assist, reflecting their focus on swift vertical progression and exploiting central channels typical for their 4-4-2 formation [#401].
- Westport Albion’s equalizer at 30' also shows a crossing play, despite their direct style, with the final assist being a cross after a build-up with 10 passes over 40 seconds, highlighting some flexibility in attack to exploit wide penetration when needed [#553].
- Kingsmoor FC's tactical change at 65' to press higher and play more direct (press increased from 0.5 to 0.68, directness 0.5 to 0.65) was aimed at chasing the game, increasing pressure and verticality, but it did not translate into chances immediately, showing challenges adapting their usually more possession-based wide play [#1187].
- Westport Albion reacted to their lead by dropping deeper and slowing tempo at 79', reducing press and line height significantly, trying to protect their advantage with a more conservative defensive block and fewer turnovers, limiting Kingsmoor's box touches in the process [#1459].
- Despite playing with 10 men after the red card at 81', Kingsmoor scored a goal at 82' from a 2-pass combination over 9.1 seconds starting from a ball regain and finished with a close-range goal from a cross, showing their reliance on wide crossing even when down a player [#1516].
